notes: A day ticket on the MVV costs about 9 EUR; the S-Bahn to the airport takes 40 minutes. For Neuschwanstein, take the Bayern-Ticket (train and bus) or a tour.
Summer temperatures are 25-30°C. Enjoy the beer gardens and the Isar, and surf at the Eisbach. Oktoberfest runs for the last 2 weeks of September (hotel prices triple).
A Mass of beer costs 15 EUR (16+ at Oktoberfest), a Brezn 2 EUR, Schweinshaxe 20 EUR. You can bring your own food to a beer garden. When tipping, round up the bill.
Weisswurst is eaten before noon and the skin is peeled off. Serve it with sweet mustard.
Museums cost 1 EUR on Sundays (the Pinakothek galleries). Book Neuschwanstein tickets online weeks ahead.
The Dachau memorial is free and open on Mondays. Be quiet and respectful.

stops.name: Marienplatz
stops.tips: Glockenspiel at 11:00 (and 12:00, plus 17:00 in summer). The New Town Hall tower lift costs 6 EUR.

stops.name: Frauenkirche
stops.tips: Cathedral with twin onion-domed towers. Look for the Devil's footprint.

stops.name: Viktualienmarkt
stops.tips: A food market since 1807. Try Weisswurst (by tradition eaten before noon), Obazda (spiced cheese spread) and the beer garden.

stops.name: Asamkirche
stops.tips: Rococo church on Sendlinger Strasse.

stops.name: Hofbräuhaus München
stops.tips: A beer hall dating from 1589: Mass (litre) beers, Schweinshaxe (roast pork knuckle) and a brass band. You share long tables with locals.

backups.name: Augustiner Bräustuben
backups.tips: The brewery's own hall, a local alternative to the Hofbräuhaus.

backups.name: St. Peter's Church Tower (Alter Peter)
backups.tips: 306 steps up to views over Marienplatz. An alternative to the Frauenkirche.

stops.name: Munich Residence
stops.tips: The Wittelsbach palace, with the Antiquarium, the treasury and the Cuvilliés Theatre.

stops.name: Hofgarten
stops.tips: Palace garden with the Temple of Diana.

stops.name: Eisbachwelle
stops.tips: Surfers ride a river wave in the middle of the city, all year round.

stops.name: Chinesischer Turm Biergarten
stops.tips: Beer garden by the Chinese pagoda in the Englischer Garten. You can bring your own food; try Brezn (pretzel) and Steckerlfisch (fish grilled on a stick).

stops.name: Englischer Garten Monopteros
stops.tips: Larger than Central Park. The Greek-style temple on the hill gives city views, and you can take a rowing boat on Lake Kleinhesselohe.

backups.name: Alte Pinakothek
backups.tips: Dürer, Rubens, Rembrandt. Entry is 1 EUR on Sundays. A good option instead of the park when it rains.

stops.name: Nymphenburg Palace
stops.tips: Baroque summer palace with the Gallery of Beauties and the Amalienburg. The park is free.

stops.name: Nymphenburg Palace Park
stops.tips: Canals and pavilions, with swans.

stops.name: Schlosscafé im Palmenhaus
stops.tips: Greenhouse café for lunch in the palace park.

stops.name: Olympiapark
stops.tips: The tent roofs of the 1972 Olympics. The Olympic Tower viewing platform costs 13 EUR.

stops.name: BMW Welt & Museum
stops.tips: BMW Welt is free and the museum costs 10 EUR. Next to Olympiapark.

backups.name: Pinakothek der Moderne
backups.tips: Modern art and design. An alternative to BMW.

stops.name: Dachau Concentration Camp Memorial Site
stops.tips: 45 minutes by S2 and bus. Memorial to the first concentration camp, free entry, audio guide 4 EUR. Heavy going, but important.

stops.name: Dachau Altstadt
stops.tips: Old town and palace garden for a quiet break.

stops.name: Schwabing Leopoldstrasse
stops.tips: Bohemian district with the Siegestor and cafés.

stops.name: Café Luitpold
stops.tips: A coffeehouse since 1888. Try the Prinzregententorte.

stops.name: Glockenbachviertel
stops.tips: Gay-friendly neighbourhood with bars and Gärtnerplatz.

backups.name: Bratwurstherzl Viktualienmarkt
backups.tips: Nuremberg sausages next to the market.

backups.name: Lenbachhaus
backups.tips: Home of the Blaue Reiter (Kandinsky, Marc). An alternative to Schwabing.

stops.name: Neuschwanstein Castle
stops.tips: 2.5 hours by train and bus (Bayern-Ticket) or on a tour. Ludwig's fairy-tale castle. Book your timed ticket online weeks ahead; the climb takes 30 minutes.

stops.name: Marienbrücke
stops.tips: The bridge with the postcard view of the castle. It may be closed in winter because of ice.

stops.name: Hohenschwangau Castle
stops.tips: Ludwig's childhood castle. Combined ticket available.

stops.name: Alpsee Lake Walk
stops.tips: Mountain lake below the castles, with swans.

stops.name: Füssen Altstadt
stops.tips: Medieval town. Try Käsespätzle (cheese noodles) before the train back.

backups.name: Tegelbergbahn
backups.tips: Cable car to an Alpine summit. An alternative to the lake.

stops.name: Deutsches Museum
stops.tips: The world's largest science and technology museum, with a mine, aircraft and a planetarium.

stops.name: Isar River Walk
stops.tips: River island and banks. In summer people swim and barbecue here.

stops.name: Wirtshaus in der Au
stops.tips: Bavarian inn specialising in Knödel (dumplings), in the Au district.

stops.name: Müllersches Volksbad
stops.tips: Art nouveau swimming pool from 1901, with a sauna.

stops.name: Gärtnerplatz
stops.tips: Round square with a theatre. Best in the evening.

backups.name: Deutsches Museum Verkehrszentrum
backups.tips: Transport museum. An alternative to the baths.

stops.name: Theresienwiese & Bavaria Statue
stops.tips: The Oktoberfest grounds (September to October). Take in the view from the head of the Bavaria statue.

stops.name: Augustiner-Keller Biergarten
stops.tips: Beer garden for 5,000 under chestnut trees. Have a Mass and a Brezn for your farewell.

stops.name: Munich Central Station
stops.tips: The S-Bahn to the airport takes 40 minutes. Farewell.

backups.name: Dallmayr
backups.tips: Luxury delicatessen and café at Marienplatz. Good for souvenirs.

backups.name: Alter Botanischer Garten
backups.tips: Park beside the station. An alternative to Theresienwiese.
